interactions.summary: Jiang pivots from the Brunetto discussion into a recap of Dante as prophet and begins mapping the characteristics of hell onto Florence and the present day.
Jiang asks why a person formed by meritocratic competition might never apologize after sabotaging a friend, and students answer in terms of ego, self-justification, and moral knowledge.

speaker_notes.note: Jiang explicitly dates Dante's warning by linking ignored prophecy to the later arrival of the Black Death.

claims.claim: Jiang says Dante builds hell as an allegory for Italy and Florence, so the geography of inferno doubles as a diagnosis of his society.
Jiang frames Dante as a prophet warning that if people do not repent, judgment will be swift and harsh, later exemplified by the Black Death.
claims.temporal_scope: Lecture chronology claim on 2026-06-23 about 1357 and after.

claims.claim: Jiang identifies factionalism and intense economic pressure to succeed as two major characteristics of Florence that continue into the present meritocracy.
Students suggest a meritocratic saboteur may refuse apology because ego and self-justification let her reinterpret her deed rather than confess it.

signature_moments.moment: Ignored prophecy is answered by plague-level judgment.
signature_moments.source_phrase: judge judgment will be swift, brutal, and harsh
signature_moments.why_it_matters: Jiang turns Dante into a civilizational warner whose claims are tested by historical catastrophe.

signature_moments.source_phrase: there is an almost incapacity to apologize
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is one of Jiang's strongest translations of infernal logic into contemporary social psychology.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's name for a system where success and achievement dominate moral life and deform ordinary human responses like apology.

chronology_notes.note: After the break, the lecture broadens from Brunetto's case into a general mapping from Dante's Florence to modern meritocratic society.

uncertainty_notes.note: Jiang names 1357 and the Black Death in a compressed way; preserve the plague reference as part of his prophetic framing without overclaiming exact chronology from this packet alone.
